title: Flat at a prime with smooth fibre implies smooth at the prime
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $\mathfrak q\subset S$ a prime ideal and $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. Let $F=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ be the fibre ring [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $\mathfrak Q\subset F$ the kernel of the ring map $F\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, $s\otimes\lambda\mapsto\bar s\bar\lambda$ (the prime of $F$ corresponding to $\mathfrak q$). Assume (1) there is $g\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that $S_g$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]; (2) the local ring map $R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$ induced by $\varphi$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; (3) $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to F$ is smooth at $\mathfrak Q$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]. Then $R\to S$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal].
